## Root cause

The two tiers are launched concurrently on two streams and both tiers call
`_fused_experts` with **the same `workspace` tensor** (the default workspace
allocated by the primary kernel and reused by every tier). Marlin's
`moe_wna16_marlin_gemm` writes scratch into that workspace. With two kernels
running at the same time on different streams, the two launches race on the
same device buffer:

* the HBM tier and the UVA tier overwrite each other's scratch, and
* because the workspace is also used to stage intermediate results, one kernel
  can read addresses the other kernel has just invalidated.

There is no inter-stream synchronization protecting that buffer, so the access
pattern is a classic unsynchronized cross-stream write-write / read-write
hazard. That is the illegal memory access.

The profile already tells you the skew is an *order statistic* (86%), not persistent imbalance. An order statistic is the `max` of N roughly-equal random variables — it exists *because* you take a max, not because any single rank is systematically heavier. Reassigning which rank owns which expert changes the *labels* on the variables but not their distribution. You still take `max` over the same number of ranks, so the expected max is unchanged.

The only way a static remap helps is if there is a persistent, exploitable anti-correlation: expert A and expert B are frequently co-active and currently on the same rank, and splitting them reduces the variance of the per-rank sum.
